$comment: Why a counting rule changed, and whether the calibration window survived it.
Spec: docs/spec/the-ratchet.md. Decision: docs/adr/0085-a-renovation-is-declared-and-the-window-may-survive.md.
Ticket: https://github.com/mephistopheles4/stacks/issues/227
A STAMP RECORDS THE RULE A NUMBER WAS PRODUCED UNDER. When a stamp moves, numbers
either side of it are not comparable, so the calibration window restarts. Before this
file, nothing anywhere said WHY it moved: a reader of the trend page met a step change
and supplied their own story. The floors files carried dated prose, which marks the
FILE and never the series.
A STAMP ENTRY names one of configHash, fixtureHash or duplicationHash, and the value
that stamp took. G57 compares it to the floors file, so a stamp that moves without an
entry here is a RED PULL REQUEST rather than a surprise at the next deploy.
A FREE ENTRY says "stamp": "none". It records a change a reader notices and no stamp
records — a formatter adoption, a Node upgrade, a rule set widened. NOTHING CAN FORCE
A FREE ENTRY, because forcing means a comparison and there is no stamp to compare
against. That is a property of the class and not a gap in the gate. #227's own table
measured that Prettier, markdownlint and extra ESLint rules move no count, and #342
removed the last version trigger — so this class is now the only home for a renovation
a reader would otherwise have no record of.
AN UNRECOGNISED STAMP NAME IS A PARSE ERROR, which is parseCaps' rule in
scripts/lib/floors.ts for the same reason: a typo must not read as something weaker.
"fixturehash" would otherwise land as a free entry, leave the real stamp unmarked, and
pass the gate.
REQUIRED ON EVERY STAMP ENTRY AND NEVER DEFAULTED. It says whether the calibration
window survives this change. A default would let *nobody decided* read as *the window
restarts*, and this flag is the whole decision the marker exists to record.
true  — runs counted under the PREVIOUS value still count toward this stamp's window.
Claim it only when the counts themselves were measured unchanged.
false — the window restarts here, which is what a stamp change has always meant.
⚠️ IT IS READ FOR TWO STAMPS OF THE THREE. configHash and fixtureHash each have a
calibration window; duplicationHash has none, because the six duplication caps are #269's
and unbuilt. So `preserves` on a duplicationHash entry is required here and read by
nothing, and a `true` there would do nothing at all today. It is required anyway: a field
required on two stamps and forbidden on the third is a rule nobody remembers. WHOEVER
LANDS #269 WIRES acceptedValues(…, 'duplicationHash', …) INTO THAT WINDOW — nothing
reddens to remind them, which is the stated cost. See ADR-0085's Consequences.
⚠️ A JSCPD BUMP IS A BOT-CAUSED RENOVATION, and it is the only one left. duplicationHash
digests the jscpd version AS INSTALLED, because a clone detector's version decides what a
clone is — so a Dependabot pull request reddens G47 and G57 together and a bot can
re-derive neither. Accepted rather than answered: G47 already reddened that build, so the
human was already required. #328 and #339 are both that case.
THE THREE SEEDED ENTRIES BELOW ARE ALL `false`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN LAZY.
They are history, and ADR-0084 landed the same day saying records are not rewritten and
every window reads 0 of 10 from that commit. Seeding them `true` would silently reverse
an ADR one day old. The mechanism applies FORWARD.
The 2026-10-09 configHash entry is the one `true` that joins a window today. It said
`false` and was corrected in place on 2026-10-17 (#464), on a measurement and the owner's
decision, while it was still the newest entry for its stamp — so the 2026-10-17
duplicationHash entry's "the first true in this file" was true when written. The store
already held the entry, so the correction cost one `pnpm trend:sync --rebuild`. An entry
older than the newest one for its stamp is never edited.
APPEND ONLY, AND FILE ORDER IS THE RECORD. The one exception is a correction to the newest
entry for a stamp, which G57's message allows and #464 made once. The newest entry for a stamp is the last one
naming it, read by position and never by date: two renovations can land on one day, and
a sort by date would pick between them by an accident of the sort's stability.

renovations.reason: G56 landed and the stamp was re-derived from the configuration it claims to describe. The scoring configuration itself did not move, so no score changed; the stamp did, because the gate that now compares it needed the file and the config to agree.
jscpd moved to 5.2.0. The installed version is an input to this stamp by design, because a clone detector's own version decides what a clone is. Measured across the bump: no duplication count moved.

The counting stamp stopped digesting the three installed versions and now holds the two rule-option sets and the two inventories. Measured: the same tree counted identically under two parser and eslint pairs, all 64 rows. This is the last version-driven refresh by construction — no dependency bump can move this stamp again.

jscpd moved to 5.3.2. Unlike 5.2.0, this bump moves a count: over the identical tree the whole-tree population goes from 53 clones and 558 duplicated lines to 55 and 619, while all eight declared scopes are unchanged. No source changed; the detector draws clone boundaries differently. Two existing test-file clones were re-segmented (update-book.test.ts against insert-body-section.test.ts, and a pair inside floors.test.ts), and two pairs are newly reported, update-book.test.ts against gates/hand-edited-notes.test.ts and a second pair inside floors.test.ts. All six spans are test files.

Two files join the shelf scope's zero-mutant residuals beside debug-panel.ts, both reached only through boot.ts: pickup-tuner.ts, the pickup tuner behind ?debug, which imports its stylesheet with Vite's ?url that only a Vite build resolves; and pickup.ts, the drawing half of picking a book up, whose rules are tested in the pure modules it calls. card-sheet.ts was deleted with the sheet and was never a residual. No declared scope's glob changed. Corrected to preserves true on 2026-10-17 (#464), on the owner's decision: both files were created in this same commit, so on every older tree their two negations match nothing. Measured: neither file exists on any of the 13 nightly trees under the previous value, 171a96f to f1c252c. On f1c252c the shelf scope run under the old and the new configuration found the same 25 files and 2688 mutants, identical mutant for mutant, with not one status different; the same construction on 3c94634 told them apart, 32 files against 30. Correcting this entry in place costs one pnpm trend:sync --rebuild, because the store already held it.

jscpd moved to 5.4.1. Measured over the identical tree, main at f322cef under 5.3.2 against the bump at cbd508b under 5.4.1, which differ only in package.json and the lockfile: no duplication count moved. The whole tree reads 69 clones, 747 duplicated lines, 88635 total lines and 0 ignored under both, all eight declared scopes are unchanged, and the 69 clone spans were diffed one by one and are identical, not only their totals. So the window is declared preserved, the first true in this file. No code reads a duplication calibration window yet, so this flag does nothing today; it is recorded so the window carries across this bump once #269's reader is wired. One gap: the tree holds no jscpd:ignore block, so how 5.4.1 handles a suppression block was not exercised.

A stale exclusion went with its file: scripts/gh-post.ts was deleted (#461), so its entry in the scripts scope's exclusions went too. Two mutated, tested modules, scripts/lib/github-body.ts and scripts/lib/github-post.ts, were deleted in the same change; that is an ordinary code change the window already sees across trees, and configHash hashes the Stryker configuration, not the files. No declared scope's glob changed. Declared preserved on 2026-10-17 on the owner's decision (q1, relayed by the head chef), which departs from the spec's preserves false. Measured on this branch's tree after the deletions, resolving stryker.config.mjs's mutate array under the old and the new stryker.scopes.json against the tracked files: both read 107 files, identical file for file, and Stryker generates a file's mutants from that file alone, so the mutant inventory is identical too. The same construction on the pre-change tree told them apart, 109 files against 110, the one difference being scripts/gh-post.ts. This compares the resolved file sets and was not a mutation run, so the scores themselves were not re-run.
